title: Reading connected clusters — full joining review
objectives: Student can read any 2–3 letter unvoweled cluster built from any combination of the 28 letters, correctly identifying each component letter regardless of its positional shape.
Student demonstrates the non-connector rule applying correctly and automatically, without needing the rule restated.
Student's cluster-reading pace has visibly increased from lesson 1.7's baseline (informal, non-graded pacing check only).

slides.heading: Lesson 1.9 — Reading connected clusters: full joining review

audio.cue: ا: an open, unobstructed sound from deep in the chest cavity — no closure anywhere, just a clear open vowel
lips fully together
tongue-tip on gum ridge
tongue between teeth
ح: a strong, breathy, unvoiced friction from the middle of the throat — like fogging a mirror from deep in the throat, no English equivalent
خ: a rasping fricative from the upper throat/back of the tongue against the soft palate — a genuine back-of-throat 'kh', not softened
د: tongue-tip taps the upper gum ridge firmly — a plain, crisp 'd'
ذ: tongue-tip between the teeth, same point as ث but VOICED — 'th' as in 'this', never a 'z'

audio.title: Arabic101 Makharij Lesson 10 — ر (ra), the ULTIMATE guide

audio.cue: ز: tip of tongue near the lower teeth, a plain buzzing 'z' — voiced twin of س
س: tip of tongue near the lower teeth, a thin hiss — a plain 's'
ش: middle of tongue against the roof of the mouth, a soft 'sh'
ع: a mid-throat muscular squeeze, voiced — no equivalent sound in English or Turkic languages
غ: upper throat, same zone as خ but voiced — a uvular fricative, like a French uvular 'r'
ف: inner lower lip against the edge of the upper front teeth — a plain 'f'
ك: back of tongue against the soft palate, shallower in the mouth than ق — a plain 'k'
م: the two lips, with nasal resonance — 'm'
ه: a light, breathy throat release — a soft 'h', much gentler than ح
و: rounded lips — a consonant 'w'
ي: middle of tongue toward the roof of the mouth — a consonant 'y'

slides.heading: Everything you need to read any cluster
body: Rule 1 (lesson 1.7): a letter's sound never changes, but its SHAPE changes by position — isolated, initial, medial, final.
Rule 2 (lesson 1.8): 6 letters — ا د ذ ر ز و — never connect forward, no matter where they sit.
That's it. Those two rules are everything needed to read any connected cluster of the 28 letters.

dailyChecklist: Write the positional forms of 2–3 tricky letters from today, 4 rows each, in your notebook, saying each position aloud as you write
Re-read the full 12-item mixed cluster set aloud, 3× through, self-timed informally

script: Open with the full 28-letter cumulative shuffle, then restate the two rules that make ALL cluster-reading possible: the 4 positional forms and the 6 non-connectors.
Run guided reading set 1 (early shape-families), then set 2 (later shape-families), then set 3 (clusters mixing non-connectors throughout) — teacher-led, correcting live.
Move to the independent reading round only after all three guided sets: present the 5 cold-read clusters and observe WITHOUT prompting unless the student is truly stuck.
Review the error log together with the student — name which letters/cluster types caused hesitation, feeding directly into Checkpoint 1 prep.
Time the pacing-check cluster set informally and frame it as encouragement (compare lightly against lesson 1.7's pace), never as a graded metric.
Close with the preview of Unit 1.3 — vowels are next, and these same letters are about to come alive.
listenFor: Any letter from the "high-risk six" (ح, ض, ع, ق, ذ/ز pattern, ص) resurfacing as an error once embedded inside a cluster rather than read in isolation — flag explicitly, this is the most diagnostic moment before Checkpoint 1.
Hesitation specifically on non-connector transitions — confirms whether lesson 1.8's rule has become automatic or still needs conscious recall.

Reading pace: increasing hesitation as cluster length grows from 2 to 3 letters may indicate the student is still sounding out letter-by-letter rather than starting to chunk — normal at this stage, just note it for Phase 2 planning.

Student keeps their own simple tally of which clusters felt hardest, to discuss at the start of lesson 1.10. No printed sheets.
